name: DRV8838 single DC motor driver
description: TI DRV8838 single H-bridge motor driver with a PHASE/ENABLE interface: runs one small brushed DC motor forwards, backwards or braked from 1.8-7 V logic, motor supply 0-11 V, up to 1.8 A peak (about 1.7 A continuous on the carrier). Sold as: Pololu DRV8838 Single Brushed DC Motor Driver Carrier (#2990), 0.4 x 0.5 in 10-pin DIP-style board; logic row GND VCC EN PH SLP, motor row GND VIN O2 O1 VM.
eli5: Lets your board spin one small motor forwards or backwards and set its speed, using a separate battery for the motor.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (logic side): shared with the microcontroller and the motor supply

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Logic supply 1.8-7 V (e.g. the microcontroller's 3V3). Sets the input thresholds; under 1.7 V the outputs switch off (UVLO)

pins.name: EN
pins.description: ENABLE: high = drive, low = brake (both outputs low). PWM it for speed (max 250 kHz). ~100 kOhm pull-down on the chip

pins.name: PH
pins.description: PHASE: direction. Low = forward (OUT1 high), high = reverse (OUT2 high). ~100 kOhm pull-down on the chip

pins.name: SLP
pins.description: nSLEEP: low = sleep, outputs off (motor coasts). 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board, so it runs if left open

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Ground (motor side, printed GND): motor supply negative

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Motor supply input through the reverse-polarity MOSFET, about 1.5-11 V. Recommended motor power pin

pins.name: O2
pins.description: Motor output OUT2; connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: O1
pins.description: Motor output OUT1; connect the motor, not the microcontroller

pins.name: VM
pins.description: Motor supply after the reverse-protection MOSFET (0-11 V). Normally an output; feed power here only for very low motor voltages

supplierQuery: Pololu DRV8838 single brushed DC motor driver carrier 2990
buildNotes: Truth table (TI datasheet Table 7-2): SLP low = coast (outputs off); EN low = brake (both outputs low); EN high with PH low = forward (OUT1 high), PH high = reverse (OUT2 high).
Speed: PWM the EN pin (up to 250 kHz; 20 kHz is silent). The motor brakes during the low part of each period.
Power the logic from VCC (1.8-7 V, e.g. the microcontroller's 3V3) and the motor from VIN (reverse-polarity protected, about 1.5-11 V). VM bypasses the protection and is normally left unconnected.
Connect the board GND to the microcontroller GND; both GND pins are the same net.
SLP has a 10 kOhm pull-up on the board, so the driver runs if SLP is left open. Drive it low only to coast or sleep.
Control inputs take at most 5.5 V (7 V absolute); never connect them to the motor supply.
No fault output: over-current (1.9 A min) and over-temperature shut the bridge off and it retries by itself. The chip gets hot above about 1 A.

driver.code:
# DRV8838 single brushed DC motor driver (TI DRV8838), MicroPython driver.
# PHASE/ENABLE interface from the TI datasheet (SLVSBA4F, Table 7-2 "DRV8838 Device Logic"):
#   nSLEEP = 0              -> OUT1/OUT2 Hi-Z: coast (sleep mode)
#   nSLEEP = 1, EN = 0      -> OUT1 L, OUT2 L: brake
#   nSLEEP = 1, PH = 0, EN = 1 -> OUT1 H, OUT2 L: forward
#   nSLEEP = 1, PH = 1, EN = 1 -> OUT1 L, OUT2 H: reverse
# Speed: PWM on EN (0-250 kHz allowed); while EN is low the outputs brake (both low).
# Inputs: VIH <= 0.5 x VCC, VIL >= 0.25 x VCC, max 5.5 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs work with VCC = 3.3 V or 5 V.
# PH and EN have ~100 kOhm pull-downs on the chip. On the Pololu carrier SLP has a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC,
# so the driver is awake unless SLP is driven low. Wake time after nSLEEP rises: tWAKE <= 30 us.
from machine import Pin, PWM
import time


class DRV8838:
    def __init__(self, ph, en, slp=None, freq=20000):
        """ph, en: GPIO numbers wired to PH and EN.
        slp: GPIO number wired to SLP (nSLEEP), or None to leave it on the board's pull-up (always awake).
        freq: PWM frequency on EN for speed control (20 kHz is above hearing; datasheet max 250 kHz)."""
        self._en_no = en
        self._freq = freq
        self._pwm = None
        self.ph = Pin(ph, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.en = Pin(en, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.slp = None
        if slp is not None:
            self.slp = Pin(slp, Pin.OUT, value=0)
            self.wake()

    def wake(self):
        """Drive nSLEEP high and wait tWAKE (30 us max)."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(1)
            time.sleep_us(30)

    def sleep(self):
        """nSLEEP low: outputs Hi-Z (the motor coasts), chip draws nanoamps.
        On the Pololu carrier the 10 kOhm pull-up then draws VCC / 10 kOhm."""
        if self.slp is not None:
            self.slp.value(0)

    def _enable(self, speed):
        speed = max(0, min(100, speed))
        if speed > 0 and self.slp is not None and not self.slp.value():
            self.wake()  # coming back from coast()
        if self._pwm is not None:
            self._pwm.deinit()
            self._pwm = None
            self.en = Pin(self._en_no, Pin.OUT)
        if speed >= 100:
            self.en.value(1)
        elif speed <= 0:
            self.en.value(0)
        else:
            # EN high = drive, EN low = brake, so the duty cycle is the speed.
            self._pwm = PWM(Pin(self._en_no), freq=self._freq, duty_u16=speed * 65535 // 100)

    def forward(self, speed=100):
        """PH low, EN high (or PWM): OUT1 high, OUT2 low. speed 0-100 %."""
        self.ph.value(0)
        self._enable(speed)

    def reverse(self, speed=100):
        """PH high, EN high (or PWM): OUT1 low, OUT2 high. speed 0-100 %."""
        self.ph.value(1)
        self._enable(speed)

    def brake(self):
        """EN low: both outputs low, the motor is shorted and stops quickly."""
        self._enable(0)

    def coast(self):
        """Outputs Hi-Z so the motor spins down freely. Needs SLP wired to a GPIO."""
        self._enable(0)
        self.sleep()

    def stop(self):
        self.brake()

example.code:
import time
from drv8838 import DRV8838

# PH sets direction, EN switches the bridge on. SLP is left open: the board's pull-up keeps the chip awake.
motor = DRV8838({PH}, {EN})
while True:
    motor.forward()
    print('motor forward')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.reverse()
    print('motor reverse')
    time.sleep(1)
    motor.brake()
    print('motor braking')
    time.sleep(1)
